verdict.rationale: CoreWeave documents its own API Access Tokens that grant access to resources, per-cluster kubeconfigs, exchange of a token for temporary AI Object Storage credentials, and bucket policies that grant or restrict access by principal or group. Together these give some resource-level least-privilege control, but nothing shows that the tokens themselves can be scoped to specific permissions or issued as agent or service identities. Missing for 10: documented per-token permission scopes or roles, service-account or agent-specific credentials, a least-privilege token-issuance workflow, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: API Access Tokens authenticate users and grant access to resources such as CKS clusters and VPCs.
Create and download a kubeconfig for a specific cluster, so you can interact with the cluster using commands like kubectl.
you can now exchange that token directly for temporary AI Object Storage credentials through the container credentials endpoint.
CoreWeave AI Object Storage bucket policies now support group-based access control, letting you grant or restrict access based on a principal's group memberships rather than listing individual users.
